title: Stat-Line & Equipment
blurb: Every figure's six stats, and the equipment rules governing item slots, weapons and armour (Chapter One, pages 25-26, 33-37).

rows.name: Move (M)
rows.text: Distance a figure may move (inches) per Move action.

rows.name: Fight (F)
rows.text: Hand-to-hand ability, and ability to avoid missile fire.

rows.name: Shoot (S)
rows.text: Missile-weapon ability (bow/crossbow); doesn't affect shooting attacks generated by spells.

rows.name: Armour (A)
rows.text: Physical protection: worn armour/shield, natural armour, and magic.

rows.name: Will (W)
rows.text: Determination and courage; used to resist spells.

rows.name: Health (H)
rows.text: Damage a figure can take before being wounded or killed.

rows.name: Split stats
rows.text: Written e.g. "+3/+2": the first number is the figure's true stat (used for level-up caps and to derive the apprentice's stat-line), the second is the current effective value used for die rolls. Occurs from magic items, spells, or permanent injuries.

rows.name: Item slots
rows.text: Wizard 5, Apprentice 4, Soldier 1 (on top of the soldier's own standard listed gear). Neither wizard nor apprentice may wear armour or carry a shield.

rows.name: Dagger
rows.text: -1 damage. The first dagger a figure carries doesn't use an item slot.

rows.name: Hand Weapon
rows.text: No modifier.

rows.name: Two-Handed Weapon
rows.text: +2 damage; takes 2 item slots.

rows.name: Staff
rows.text: -1 damage for its wielder; also gives whoever it fights in melee (not shooting) a -1 damage modifier. Includes magic staffs.

rows.name: Bow
rows.text: Load and fire in a single action; 24" maximum range; needs a quiver (or magic ammunition) to use.

rows.name: Crossbow
rows.text: +2 damage. Load and fire are separate actions (reloading may replace the move action instead); 24" maximum range; assumed loaded at the start of a game; needs a quiver (or magic ammunition) to use.

rows.name: Quiver
rows.text: Required to shoot a bow or crossbow (unless carrying magic ammunition instead). May also carry one piece of magic ammunition for free (no extra slot).

rows.name: Unarmed
rows.text: -2 Fight, -2 damage. A creature with no weapon listed in its notes fights with natural weapons and is never counted as unarmed.

rows.name: Shield
rows.text: +1 Armour. Can't be combined with a two-handed weapon or a staff. Spellcasters may not carry one.

rows.name: Light Armour
rows.text: +1 Armour. Spellcasters may not wear it.

rows.name: Heavy Armour
rows.text: +2 Armour, -1 Move. Spellcasters may not wear it.

rows.name: Maximum Armour
rows.text: A permanent warband member's Armour stat is capped at 15 (excess is reduced to 15). Creatures are exempt, even as temporary warband members.

rows.name: Magic weapons/armour on soldiers
rows.text: A soldier may only carry/wear a magic version of a weapon or armour type it's already listed with (e.g. a dagger-armed thief can only use a magic dagger, never a magic hand weapon or any armour) — it replaces the mundane item and still fills the soldier's one item slot.

title: Warband Composition & Creatures
blurb: Building and maintaining a warband (Chapter One pages 26-32; Chapter Three page 103).

rows.name: Starting gold
rows.text: 400gc for a newly created wizard.

rows.name: Hiring an apprentice
rows.text: 100gc for a wizard's first apprentice. Optional — going without one doesn't raise the soldier cap.

rows.name: Roster cap
rows.text: Max 8 soldiers, of which up to 4 may be specialists. A base or resource (e.g. Inn, Kennel) can add specific, limited exceptions.

rows.name: Soldier standard gear
rows.text: Listed per soldier type; replaced free automatically if lost during play. Can't be supplemented from the General Arms and Armour list — only via the soldier's own one item slot.

rows.name: Removing a soldier or apprentice
rows.text: No refund; any magic item the soldier was carrying may be kept by the warband.

rows.name: Creatures in warbands
rows.text: A spell or item states whether a creature joins temporarily (an extra figure for one game only, doesn't count toward roster size) or permanently (takes a soldier slot — standard or specialist as stated — and stays until dismissed or killed). Creatures have no item slots and can't carry items, but may carry treasure unless stated otherwise, and activate in the Soldier phase like any soldier unless stated otherwise.

rows.name: Control-spell limit
rows.text: Control Construct/Undead/Animal/Demon: a spellcaster may control only one creature of each type at a time. Permanent warband members never count against this limit, even if the same type (e.g. a warband construct doesn't stop its wizard from also Controlling a different construct that game).

title: Post-Game: Injury & Death
blurb: The Survival Roll procedure for anyone reduced to 0 Health or less in a campaign game (a one-off game just treats 0 Health as dead) (Chapter Three, pages 73-79).

rows.name: Soldier Survival Table (d20)
rows.text: 1-4 Dead (removed; any carried items are lost) · 5-8 Badly Wounded (misses the next game, then returns at full Health) · 9+ Full Recovery (returns next game at full Health).

rows.name: Spellcaster Survival Table (d20, wizard may add +1 after rolling)
rows.text: 1-2 Dead · 3-4 Permanent Injury (roll below) · 5-6 Badly Wounded (miss a game, or pay 150gc for treatment — 100gc discount with an apothecary in the warband; may go into debt but can't spend gold until it's paid off) · 7-8 Close Call (survives, but loses every carried item — General Arms and Armour items are replaced free) · 9+ Full Recovery.

rows.name: Permanent Injury Table (d20)
rows.text: 1-2 Lost Toes · 3-6 Smashed Leg · 7-10 Crushed Arm · 11-12 Lost Fingers · 13-14 Never Quite as Strong · 15-16 Psychological Scars · 17-18 Niggling Injury · 19 Smashed Jaw · 20 Lost Eye. (The 2e rulebook prints Crushed Arm's range as "6-10", overlapping Smashed Leg's top end by one — shown here as 7-10 so the 20 slots add up without a gap.)

rows.name: Lost Toes
rows.text: -1 to all Move Rolls. A second result stacks to -2; any further result is re-rolled.

rows.name: Smashed Leg
rows.text: -2 Move. A second result stacks to -4; any further result is re-rolled.

rows.name: Crushed Arm
rows.text: -1 Fight. A second result stacks to -2; any further result is re-rolled.

rows.name: Lost Fingers
rows.text: -1 Shoot. A second result stacks to -2; any further result is re-rolled.

rows.name: Never Quite as Strong
rows.text: Starts every game at -1 Health. A second result stacks to -2; any further result is re-rolled.

rows.name: Psychological Scars
rows.text: -1 Will. A second result stacks to -2; any further result is re-rolled.

rows.name: Niggling Injury
rows.text: 30gc upkeep before each game, or start that game at -3 Health instead (10gc discount per apothecary in the warband). A second result raises this to 40gc/-4 Health; any further result is re-rolled.

rows.name: Smashed Jaw
rows.text: May only activate 2 soldiers per phase instead of the normal 3. A second result drops this to 1; any further result is re-rolled.

rows.name: Lost Eye
rows.text: -1 Combat Roll when targeted by a shooting attack. A second Lost Eye on the same figure leaves it effectively blind — if Miraculous Cure isn't cast successfully to remove it during that same post-game's Out of Game Spells step, the figure retires and is treated as "dead" for game purposes.

rows.name: Recording an injury
rows.text: Write it in the figure's notes. A stat-affecting injury is recorded as a split stat (e.g. Fight +3 with a Crushed Arm becomes +3/+2): the first number is the figure's true stat, the second is what's actually rolled with.

title: Experience & Level
blurb: Only wizards earn XP — apprentices and soldiers don't. Every full 100 XP may be converted into a level whenever the player chooses; XP can be banked (Chapter Three, pages 82-84).

rows.name: Experience sources
rows.text: +5 per failed spell-casting attempt that damages the caster · +10 per spell successfully cast (none for a casting number of 6 or less) · +40 for participating in a game · +40 per treasure token secured · +5 per uncontrolled creature killed (max +50/game; excludes creatures with their own scenario XP reward, or ones summoned/created by the warband itself).

rows.name: Per-game XP cap
rows.text: 300, from in-game sources. Out of Game spells never grant XP.

rows.name: Per level, choose one
rows.text: Improve a stat by +1 (cap Fight +5, Shoot +5, Will +8, Health 20 — only one stat per game even with several levels banked) · lower one known spell's casting number by -1 (floor of 5, regardless of school relation; only one spell per game) · learn a new spell from a grimoire already in the vault (as many new spells as levels-and-grimoires allow, but a just-learned spell can't also be improved until another game is played).

rows.name: Apprentice auto-advances
rows.text: Whenever the wizard's stat-line changes, the apprentice's derived stats update to match; the apprentice always knows the same spells as the wizard.

title: Spending Treasure & Recruitment
blurb: After Counting Treasure (the roll itself is the Treasure Table under the Loot tables card's Core Rules section) (Chapter Three, pages 103-104).

rows.name: Hiring soldiers
rows.text: Pay the listed retainer cost; limited only by the roster cap (8 total / 4 specialists).

rows.name: New apprentice cost
rows.text: (wizard level − 6) × 10 + 160gc — 100gc for a starting (level 0) wizard, rising with level.

rows.name: Wizard death
rows.text: Level 5 or less: discard the warband and start over. Level 6+: may instead promote the apprentice to wizard (new level = old wizard's level − 6, keeping the apprentice's current stats and spells); the old wizard's own carried items are lost, but everything else (other members' items, the vault) passes to the new wizard.

rows.name: Buying
rows.text: Grimoire (any spell, player's choice) 500gc · scroll 250gc · potions/magic weapons/armour/items at their listed price. No identification roll is needed for a purchase.

rows.name: Selling
rows.text: Grimoire of an already-known spell 200gc (a grimoire for an unknown spell may never be sold) · scroll 30gc · other treasure at its listed sale price.

rows.name: Optional Rule: Black Market Contacts
rows.text: Instead of open buying, each player rolls 4x on the Treasure Table after a game (ignore any gc in the results) and resolves the sub-tables to see exactly what's on offer this time; a player may only buy from their own results. One of the four rolls may be swapped for a roll on a supplement's own treasure table if that book is in use.
